entries.title: II Kings 13:2
segments: The sins of transgressors may be imitated long after they are dead, and be instrumental in the destruction of their distant posterity.

entries.title: II Kings 13:4
segments: Cries to the Lord for help may be the means of deliverance from evil and of the reception of temporal good, even where the heart is not right with him, nor the life devoted to his service.

entries.title: II Kings 13:5
segments: A savior; Joash the son of Jehoahaz, whose victories over the Syrians are recorded in the latter part of this chapter.

entries.title: II Kings 13:11
segments: No temporal favors, without the grace of God, will induce men to break off their sins, or lead them to walk in the ways of the Lord.

entries.title: II Kings 13:14
segments: The chariot--and the horsemen; he who was the defence of Israel. See note to

. 
 
The expected removal of the righteous is often lamented even by the wicked, under the conviction that their pious lives are a great blessing to mankind.

entries.title: II Kings 13:17
segments: Aphek; a city of Israel which the Syrians had taken.

entries.title: II Kings 13:18
segments:
He smote thrice; this marked the number of times that he would beat the Syrians. 
 
Strong confidence in God is needful in order to the reception, to the fullest extent, of his favors.

entries.title: II Kings 13:20
segments: Moabites; a people south-east of Judea.

entries.title: II Kings 13:21
segments:
A band; of the Moabites. 
 
  He revived; showing that God was with Elisha after his death, as really as before. 
 
The presence of God with his people is not confined to this life; and in answer to their prayers while here, he may after they are dead bestow great blessings on his people.

entries.title: II Kings 13:23
segments: Wicked men are often spared in life and made the recipients of many great and precious blessings, in consequence of the piety and benevolence of those who have gone before them.
